newsitem.title: GERMANY: Derivatives trade drives IBIS DAX index higher.
newsitem.headline: Derivatives trade drives IBIS DAX index higher.

text.p: German IBIS DAX index advanced over half a percent in pre-bourse trade on Tuesday and dealers said most of the buying interest was coming from the futures market, with buyers in the cash market hugging the sidelines.
By 0729 GMT the IBIS DAX index was up 20 points at 3,616.40 points, a rise of 0.56 percent, while the June DAX future was up nine points at 3,616 points.

"We had been expecting a weaker market, but the futures side has lifted the market. There is very little going on in the cash market, really. The improvement in the bond market is helping us," a Frankfurt trader said.
"Wall Street closed a bit lower, but that is not having a major influence this morning. We are looking now to U.S. indicators this afternoon for some direction," he said.
Regarding the row between the German government and the Bundesbank was concerned, dealers were happy for stalemate too prevail for the time being.
"Things will be okay as long as there are no new statements on the issue," a trader said.
The stand-off between finance minister Theo Waigel and the Bundesbank over the revaluation of assets has had an unsteadying effect on market sentiment over recent days.

The market was taking a close look at construction shares early on after the builder Hochtief AG and Deutsche Bank said that they were giving up plans to pool their stake in construction firm Philipp Holzmann AG.
Both said in a statement they no longer wanted to pursue the plan after they learned the European Commission would pass the case on to German cartel authorities.

Holzmann shares were the biggest losers in early trade, down 15 marks, or 2.97 percent, at 490 marks, followed closely by Hochtief, the morning's second-biggest loser, down 60 pfennigs, or 0.80 percent, at 74 marks.
Deutsche Bank AG underperformed the overall index, rising 20 pfennigs, around 0.2 percent, to 96.72 marks.
Generally the banking sector was popular early on, with Commerzbank up 65 pfennigs, or 1.34 percent, at 49 marks, while Bayerische Vereinsbank was up 60 pfennigs, or 0.84 percent at 72 marks.
The spotlight also fell on engineer Thyssen AG, up seven marks at 400, which was due to hold an analysts's conference later on.
The stronger dollar helped to boost car stocks, most notably market darling Volkswagen AG.
Volkswagen shares were up 16.30 marks, or 1.45 percent, at 1,142 marks.
Shares in the carmaker have risen by over 82 percent from their January level of 626.50 marks.
